correctness.rationale: For binary index i, take the state pair (parity of adjacent 11, last bit), encoded 0=(0,0), 1=(0,1), 2=(1,1), 3=(1,0). Appending a 0 preserves the parity and sets last bit zero; appending a 1 adds the old last bit and sets last bit one. These are precisely the stated uniform images, proving the sequence identification. All eight state pairs occur by the fourth substitution and expanding these pairs introduces no other pairs. Every length-2^k window meets at most two aligned blocks of length 2^k; each allowed pair really occurs, so the eight concatenations with offsets 0 through 2^k give exactly the infinite word's factor set. The separate exact replay at /workspace/branches/8bdc29b3-6289-4e2b-8b53-2f5c60787748/independent_replay.py uses fixed-width integer factor keys and exact lexicographic least rotations, with no probabilistic equality. Its class sizes count represented factors, not cyclic positions. /workspace/branches/8bdc29b3-6289-4e2b-8b53-2f5c60787748/replay_4_13.txt lines 3–12 give all ten complete rows and line 13 gives REPLAY_OK. Endpoint rows (n, factor total, class total, singleton, double, full) are (16,120,58,52,2,4) and (8192,65528,32762,32756,2,4). The replay tests that no other class sizes occur. The frozen C++ verifier was inspected, not run. This is exhaustive only for k=4 through 13, with no inference outside the range.

value.rationale: Rudin–Shapiro is a standard substitution word and occupancy of represented necklaces distinguishes nearly rigid factors from freely rotatable ones. The ten substitution-aligned scales give a reproducible exact benchmark for the intermediate cases that ordinary factor complexity and Lie complexity omit: only two partial classes contain more than one factor at each scale. The highest scale is a computational cutoff, not a claimed structural threshold; the value is in the complete aligned census rather than in guessing an infinite law.
